svg.title: ThingsBoard release-3.6 - failure recovery and observability

g.text: ThingsBoard release-3.6 - failure recovery and observability
Successful processing and explicit commit boundary
Default Main SKIP_ALL_FAILURES passes false, so its late
callback remains valid and Rule Node work may continue after commit.
Retry strategies and SKIP_ALL_FAILURES_AND_TIMED_OUT pass true.
next poll() without seek or pack resubmit
Consumer position is already after the failed pack.
A later higher-offset commit may cross it; restart/rebalance before
that commit may instead redeliver from the old committed offset.
The database/external effect and queue offset are not one transaction.
Success followed by process death before commit allows redelivery.
Idempotency belongs to the Rule Node and target data model.
Failure, timeout, in-memory reprocess, and final skip
Timeout does not cancel Actor or Rule Node work.
Late callbacks can arrive after cleanup. They are invalid only when
retries=0 and failurePercentage=0, so no retry-count limit.
cleanup old context; validity is strategy-dependent
No application DLQ write occurs here.
Remaining failed or timed-out payloads are not durably recorded as attempts.
Crash A: after side effect, before broker commit
Crash B: after poll, before side effect
redeliver if provider retained unconfirmed record
There is no common seek, nack, or DLQ call.
Kafka position and committed offset now differ;
later commit or restart/rebalance determines the observed outcome.
